why_this_file_exists: The .picks corpus cannot distinguish 'the job never fired' from 'the job ran and never reached the write'. Both leave an empty directory. Separating them takes scheduler state, which lives outside the corpus and behind sources that rotate. This file carries that state with its receipts quoted verbatim, so a reviewer who can no longer reach the logs can still check the claim.

firing_signature.description: What a slate run looks like in the profile log. The MLB daily slate is cron job c9452052719c and emits one 'Running job' line per fire.

per_date_counts.description: Counts over the whole window, so the 08-19 zero is read against a denominator rather than on its own. running_job counts EVERY vig cron job, not just the slate. mem_trim is the profile's memory-trim heartbeat and is the liveness control: it proves the logger was writing on a day with no job lines.

2026-08-19.basis: An ABSENCE argument, so it is stated with its denominator. The claim is that no vig cron job of any kind started on 2026-08-19. Three things make that absence meaningful rather than a gap in the record: the log is continuous across the day (the rotation boundaries are 08-12 17:05 and 08-20 02:16, both outside it); the logger was demonstrably writing throughout, at 1727 mem_trim heartbeat lines — MORE than 08-18's 1698 and 08-20's 1726; and the neighbouring dates both show the firing signature, 2 running_job lines each. An independent source outside the host agrees: the delivery channel has zero messages on 08-19 and at least one on every other date in the window. WHY it did not fire is NOT answerable from any of these sources and is left open.

controls.quoting_convention: Every quote below is verbatim EXCEPT that an absolute home prefix is rendered as /home/<account>/. The repo's own test_deployed_scripts_and_docs_have_no_baked_in_home refuses a literal /home/<name> in a committed doc, and that guard has caught two real defects — including the first draft of this report's sibling artifact — so it is honoured rather than widened. The accounts are named in the surrounding text and the substitution is mechanical.
controls.the_08_20_contrast: 2026-08-20's slate run ended reason=text_response(finish_reason=stop) at 15:36:56,455 — a normal completion — while 08-12, 08-13 and 08-14 all ended max_iterations_reached(30/30). The cap is what distinguishes the unwritten days from the ones that wrote, and the contrast is visible in the same field of the same log line.
controls.root_only_dates: Across all 21 dates, 2026-08-20 is the only date the primary (runtime) root lacks and another root has. Ten further dates sit in exactly one root in the OTHER direction — the developer checkout stopped being written to after 2026-08-22 — and those are not misses. The enumeration blind side was one day wide, and that is a measured result over both trees, not an assumption.
workdir_lines: The slate job's recorded workdir moves twice across the window: clawdbot/sports-picks-skill on 08-11..08-15, sauce_packets/sports-picks-skill on 08-16..08-18, sauce_packets/sports-picks-runtime from 08-20 on. The clawdbot home does not exist on the host (ls: cannot access: No such file or directory), yet 08-11 and 08-15 both produced artifacts — so the recorded workdir is NOT the path the writes resolved to, and no claim in this file depends on it being so.

open_questions.question: Why did no vig cron job fire on 2026-08-19? The profile log shows the scheduler silent for the whole day while hermes itself kept logging, and none of the sources above records a reason.
open_questions.why_unanswerable: The durable execution DB is a 1000-row ring that no longer reaches the date, cron_incidents is empty, and the run journal was deployed after the fact. Answering it needs scheduler-side state that no longer exists.

open_questions.question: Why did the 2026-08-20 slate run write into the sports-picks-skill checkout when the scheduler recorded `using workdir /home/<account>/projects/sports-picks-runtime`? The run's own workdir line and the artifact's location disagree. See controls.workdir_lines for the quoted lines.
open_questions.why_unanswerable: The logs record the workdir the job was launched with, never the path the write resolved to. This is not a workdir-follows-write story in general: 08-11 through 08-15 ran with a workdir under an account home that does not exist on the host at all, and 08-11 and 08-15 still produced artifacts. Whatever resolves the write root is not the cron workdir, and this report does not guess at it.
